source.paraphrase: Requirements are definitely dumb; it does not matter who gave them to you. Every requirement must come from a person with a name, not a department.

invariants.why: Anonymous type and linter suppressions hide defects behind unaccountable shortcuts. A requirement to bypass safety must have a clear named owner.
invariants.fixHint: Attribute the suppression to an owner or issue tracker (e.g. @ts-expect-error(owner) or eslint-disable -- owner: reason), or fix the underlying type/lint error.
invariants.avoid: Bare @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck, or eslint-disable without an attributed owner.

source.locator: Step 2: Delete the part or process step
source.paraphrase: If you are not adding things back 10% of the time, you are not deleting enough. Bias is always towards adding steps 'in case'.

invariants.why: A try-catch block that only catches an exception and rethrows it unchanged is a redundant process step that adds noise and churn without value.
invariants.fixHint: Delete the redundant try/catch wrapper and let the caller receive the exception naturally.
invariants.avoid: Wrapping statements in try { ... } catch (err) { throw err; } 'just in case'.

source.paraphrase: The most common error of a smart engineer is to optimize a thing that should not exist. Only simplify after you have deleted.

invariants.why: An else block following a return or throw statement adds gratuitous nesting and complexity to control flow.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the else keyword, outdent the alternate block, and use early return guard clauses.
invariants.avoid: Keeping else blocks when the preceding if branch terminates execution.

source.paraphrase: Move faster! But you may only accelerate cycle time after you have worked on the first three steps.

invariants.why: Synchronous blocking I/O calls stall the single-threaded event loop, serializing tasks and destroying cycle time and throughput.
invariants.fixHint: Use non-blocking asynchronous APIs (e.g., node:fs/promises) with await instead of synchronous calls.
invariants.avoid: Using readFileSync, writeFileSync, or execSync in application runtime paths.

source.paraphrase: The final step is automate. Only automate after you have designed, simplified, and deleted. And never bypass automated verification.

invariants.why: Skipping or focusing tests in automated suites creates false confidence by silently dropping regression coverage.
invariants.fixHint: Remove .skip, .only, fit, or xit modifiers so all automated tests run to completion.
invariants.avoid: Leaving test.skip or it.only in committed test suites. Not reported: Playwright's runtime skip test.skip(condition, reason) called inside a test body, hook or describe callback, when the condition reads a runtime value (an identifier, member access, call or await) and the reason is a string; from a describe callback it conditionally skips the whole group, which is accepted. A top-level test.skip(cond, reason), a literal or always-true condition (true, 1, !0, !!1, an object, array, new expression, sequence, spread or function, also in parentheses or a cast), test.skip(title, fn), it.skip(...) and every .only stay reported. Known gaps: an always-true condition that still names a value (true || x, a const holding true), Mocha's TDD-UI test.skip(titleVar, 'reason'), and test.describe.skip / test.describe.only, which this check does not match (TDD-FOCUS-001 does).
